subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: Session Management Flaws
description: A quick, practical guide to Session Management Flaws.

hook.text: A user logs out. Their session token still works. Anyone with it can impersonate them for hours.

buildup.text: Sessions track who's logged in. Poor management lets attackers hijack or reuse expired sessions.

discovery.text: Secure sessions expire on logout, rotate tokens after login, and bind to client fingerprints.

twist.text: Sessions stored only in cookies without server validation can be forged if the secret key leaks.

climax.text: Testing finds sessions surviving logout. A server-side invalidation fix kills them immediately.

punchline.text: Logout must destroy the session. Not just the cookie.

quiz.question: What should happen to a session on logout?
